::: {.why}
Day 27 gave you the answer from the outside; now you have measured latency, impact and capacity yourself, so the answer can be quantitative instead of received.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the horizon range and the capacity range in which you are not competing with a faster or larger participant.
- Name the two advantages you have that are not about speed or capital.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Draw the map: horizon on one axis from microseconds to months, capital on the other from thousands to billions, with regions marked for who operates where and why. Place your own strategies on it using your measured numbers rather than assumptions.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} State the two real advantages with evidence: no capacity constraint means you can hold positions whose capacity is far too small for a fund, and no external capital means no redemption risk, so you can hold through a drawdown that would end a fund. Quantify the first by finding a signal in your book whose capacity is below any professional threshold.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the honest counterpart: what you cannot do, which is anything requiring data you cannot buy, latency you cannot achieve, or a research team.
:::
:::

::: {.deliverable}
The horizon-against-capital map with your own strategies placed on it, plus the quantified small-capacity advantage.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Name one signal in your book whose capacity is too small for a fund to bother with, and say what that is worth to you.
:::
